points.description: Mentions abstraction as an advantage of object-oriented programming: hiding or ignoring unnecessary implementation detail and focusing on the essential features of an object. Accept equivalent wording such as 'abstraction', 'hides complexity', 'models real-world essentials', or 'lets you focus on what an object does rather than how'.
points.partial_credit: Award part marks if the answer gives only a vague benefit such as 'makes programs simpler/easier to understand' without linking it to hiding detail or focusing on essentials.

levels.says: Gives a vague programming benefit such as simplicity or understandability, but does not clearly state abstraction, hiding detail, or focusing on essential features.

points.description: Mentions reusability as an advantage of object-oriented programming: code, classes, or objects can be reused in other programs or parts of a program. Accept equivalent wording such as 'reusability', 'reuse of code', 'classes can be reused', or 'avoids rewriting the same code'.
points.partial_credit: Award part marks if the answer gives only a vague benefit such as 'saves time' or 'saves effort' without clearly linking it to reusing code, classes, or objects.

levels.says: Gives a vague benefit such as saving time or effort, but does not clearly state that code, classes, or objects can be reused.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both advantages named in the model answer: abstraction and reusability, in any wording. Part marks are available where the answer gives only a vague benefit without clearly identifying abstraction or reusability. No marks are given for unrelated advantages not stated in the model answer.
